search_log: Searched the verified title and authors with first person, third person, narrator, point of view, excerpt, and first chapter terms.
Opened the Quercus publisher page; its review material identified roving points of view and a gossipy collective voice, though its displayed page did not expose the advertised excerpt directly.
Opened and inspected the sustained BingeBooks opening excerpt, which is third-person narration focalized through Audre.

Searched for the exact Goodreads first-person quotations; results reproduced the quotations but did not recover enough surrounding text to determine whether they are narration, speech, direct thought, or embedded material.

Searched specifically for collective first-person, Tiffin Talks, Greek chorus, and chapter structure; SuperSummary explicitly documented shifting third-person narration alternating with recurring collective-first-person Tiffin Talks sections.
Reviewed later-section summaries to confirm that shifting third-person narration continues beyond the opening and that the mixed structure is not merely an opening effect.
person_note: The book alternates sustained narrative persons: most scenes use roving third-person limited narration, while recurring chapters titled 'Tiffin Talks' use a participating collective first-person we. The opening material and several quote narration beats corroborate the third-person strand. The isolated first-person-singular Goodreads quotations may be local speech, thought, posts, or chapel remarks, but this does not undermine the documented recurring first-person-plural chapters. The classification is ALTERNATING; confidence is medium because the whole-book configuration is supported by commercial analysis and publisher-carried review descriptions rather than authorized sustained excerpts of both strands.
